title.en: To the Tune Rumengling: I Often Remember the Pavilion by the Stream

edition.en: Text as given on Chinese Wikisource. Lines broken at the punctuation for reading; text unchanged.
edition.zh: 据维基文库。按标点分行，文字未改。

source.name: Wikisource
source.url: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/如夢令_(李清照)/如夢令_(常記溪亭日暮)

basis.en: Song dynasty lyric (ci); the author died around 1155.
basis.zh: 宋词，作者约卒于 1155 年。

note.en: Usually read as one of Li Qingzhao’s earliest lyrics, written in her youth, long before the hard years. It is the memory of a single evening: too much wine, a wrong turn into the lotus, and a flock of birds bursting up from the water. Few poems in any language catch the laughter of being lost so exactly.
note.zh: 一般认为是李清照最早的词作之一，写于少女时代，远在后来的艰难岁月之前。它是一个傍晚的回忆：喝多了酒，误入藕花深处，一滩鸥鹭忽然从水面惊飞。很少有诗能把迷路时的笑声捕捉得这样准确。

excerpt.orig: 爭渡，爭渡，驚起一灘鷗鷺。
excerpt.en: Row hard, row hard, / and up from the shoal flew a startle of gulls and egrets.
excerpt.zh: 争渡，争渡，惊起一滩鸥鹭。

gloss.en: I often remember; some read 常 as 嘗, ‘once’.
gloss.zh: 常记：时常记起。一说“常”通“尝”，曾经。

gloss.en: 爭 is 怎, ‘how’: how to get through? Others read it as racing to row across. Both readings are old.
gloss.zh: 争渡：怎么渡过去，“争”通“怎”；一说是奋力划船抢渡。
鸥鹭：鸥鸟和白鹭，泛指水鸟。
